messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: barplot inside a function does not work, line by line works
parts:
Hi:

Here are a couple of ways you could go. Neither requires a loop and
the function is short. The work is done up front in arranging the
data. Given your table1 (thank you for the dput()), the first line
selects out the variables whose names end in 'percent' using a regular
expression. An agegp factor is then defined from the rownames and its
levels ordered. Next, table2 is created by melting table1a. The plot
function is pretty simple - it takes a generic data frame d as input.
Notice the print() wrapper around the ggplot() call; this is necessary
when you call ggplot() within a function. See R FAQ 7.22 for the
reason why. The function d_ply() will apply the function to each
subgroup (here, variable), yielding a plot for each - in other words,
it does the iteration by variable without having to explicitly loop.

table1 <- structure(list(population = c(215L, 881L, 1839L, 1396L),
pop.percent = c(5L, 20L, 43L, 32L), sample = c(25L, 102L, 240L,
185L), sa.percent = c(5L, 18L, 43L, 34L)), .Names = c("population",
"pop.percent", "sample", "sa.percent"), class = "data.frame",
row.names = c("Under35", "35-44", "45-54", "55andolder"))

table1a <- table1[, grep('percent$', names(table1))]
table1a$agegp <- factor(rownames(table1a),
levels = c('Under35', '35-44', '45-54', '55andolder'))
table2 <- melt(table1a, id = 'agegp')

plotfun <- function(d) {
print(
ggplot(d, aes(x = agegp, y = value)) + geom_bar() +
labs(x = 'Age group', y = 'Relative frequency') +
opts(title = as.character(unique(d$variable)))
)
}
d_ply(table2, .(variable), plotfun)

# You can also put both bar charts on the same page by faceting on variable;

ggplot(table2, aes(x = agegp, y = value)) + geom_bar() +
labs(x = 'Age group', y = 'Relative frequency') +
facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol = 1)

HTH,
Dennis
